name: Colombia
snapshot: Colombia swung from its first leftist president to Abelardo de la Espriella, a millionaire lawyer who promised a Bukele-style crackdown on armed groups.
culture: Colombia is the land of Gabriel García Márquez's magical realism, vallenato accordion music and cumbia, and global pop stars Shakira, Karol G and J Balvin. Medellín's transformation from cocaine capital to innovation hub is a national story. Coffee culture, salsa in Cali and Barranquilla's carnival are sources of pride.
society: A 2016 peace deal disarmed the FARC guerrillas after 50 years of war, but dissident factions, the ELN and the Clan del Golfo cartel still fight over coca and mining areas. Colombia remains the world's largest cocaine producer. It has taken in nearly three million Venezuelans. Inequality and land ownership are long-running grievances.
situation: In 2022, Colombia elected its first left-wing president, the former guerrilla Gustavo Petro, who promised "total peace" through talks with every armed group in the country. Four years later, with those talks largely failed and violence rising, Colombians swung hard the other way.

Abelardo de la Espriella, a 47-year-old millionaire criminal defence lawyer with his own clothing and rum brands, who has never held office, campaigned as "The Tiger" on a Bukele-style plan to fight armed groups and build ten mega-prisons. Endorsed by Trump, he won the 21 June runoff with 49.66 percent to 48.70 percent for Iván Cepeda, Petro's chosen successor, a margin of about 250,000 votes out of nearly 26 million (Edelman). The result was a clear rejection of Petro's government; Cepeda conceded after a recount and took the Senate seat reserved for the runner-up (AP via KOB). It was also a historic first: no far-right candidate had won Colombia's presidency in its modern history, while Cepeda's 12.7 million votes were the most ever for the left (Finance Colombia). De la Espriella, who once represented Maduro associate Alex Saab, took office on 7 August. A country nearly split in half now waits to see whether a hard line brings the security that dialogue did not.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single four-year term, with re-election banned, and holds strong executive powers; Congress has a Senate and a House of Representatives.
holders: President Abelardo de la Espriella (Defensores de la Patria), in office since 7 August 2026.
